newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan jails air force officer for smuggling.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan jails air force officer for smuggling.

text.p: The Pakistan Air Force (PAF) said on Friday a military court had found one flying officer guilty of masterminding a smuggling cartel and sentenced him to be dismissed and serve 10 years of hard labour in jail.

A PAF statement said Flight Lieutenant Masud-ur-Rehman had "masterminded a cartel for smuggling of electronic items by misusing official channels" while serving as officer in charge of a department at an aeronautical complex in Karachi.
"He was in league with certain civilian smugglers who are since absconding," it said.
"The other service personnel accused in this case have already been identified and will be proceeded against by court martial," the statement said.
"The civilians accused in this case will be tried by customs intelligence in a civil court of law," it said.

The rare conviction of a Pakistani military officer for smuggling follows the arrest of a senior PAF officer, Squadron Leader Mohammad Farooq, in the United States by drug officials in April for allegedly carrying two kg (4.4 lbs) of heroin in his PAF Boeing 707 aircraft.
Farooq was in the United States to bring spares for the U.S.-supplied F-16 fighters.
A second PAF officer was arrested in Pakistan after PAF chief Air Chief Marshal Abbas Khattak ordered a high-level inquiry into the incident.
